races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Race
Dino Day At Fairyhouse On July 8th Apprentice Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with an excellent Good ground 6f profile — won over C&D conditions earlier this season and his hist confirms consistent engagement on this surface; Sam Coen's 2lb claim is a genuine help at the weights, and the 19-day freshener looks ideal.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse who has finished placed over 6f on Good ground but whose best recent form has come over 5f; the tongue-tie is retained and Keithen Kennedy rides, but this trip and the likelihood of being buried deep in an 18-runner field makes this tough.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a poor recent form string of 9-0-0-9-0 that offers little encouragement; the 28-day break is notable and the tongue-tie is back on, but the historical pattern on Good ground is of a horse finishing mid-pack rather than threatening.

runners_data.name: Lady Kelly
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and a three-year-old filly who has predominantly raced over 7f-10f — she drops sharply in trip and has a going concern on Good to Firm based on just 1 sim-going run from five; she is likely to fade late, as the flag in her profile suggests, but her pace-setting role makes her dangerous to ignore early.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer from Charles Weld's yard who has placed three times on Good-ish ground across his career; the 19-day turnaround is fine, but recent form shows he has been finishing 7th-12th consistently and the big field complicates his position.

runners_data.name: Tara Na Ri
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist from Noel Meade who has been running over longer trips (8f-10f) and dropping back to 6f for the first time in recent outings; the fade flag is a concern, and Emily Grifferty's 7lb claim cannot fully offset the step down in distance from her usual stamina-based performances.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse wearing a visor, dropping back to 6f after running over 5f and 7f; the fade flag is consistent with a horse who may not see out the trip strongly, and the form string 9-0-4-7-0-8 on similar going suggests this is a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old who has placed twice on Good ground over 6f and has shown the ability to be competitive from off the pace; finishing 3rd and 2nd in recent 6f runs on Good is encouraging and Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim is a bonus.

runners_data.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran running prominently in a visor, with a placed effort over 6f on Good ground in the recent past; at OR 48 with age working against him and a trainer with no runners in the last 14 days, this is likely a place-dependent chance rather than a winning one.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent runner who won over 6f on Good ground within the last five runs and has multiple placed efforts on similar going — the p headgear is retained; Chris Timmons' yard has no recent form boost but the horse's own record makes him one of the more interesting profiles in this field.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse wearing a hood and tongue-tie, placed over 5f on Soft recently, who drops up slightly in trip; the 7-day turnaround is sharp and Wesley Joyce rides, but the sim-going record is 0 wins from 14 which tempers confidence even if the position is manageable.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse at heart — his two placed efforts have come from off the pace — but with five or more hold-up runners in this field he is mapped to midfield where he will race out of role; the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is a real discount and the 16-runner exposure in big fields historically has hurt him.

runners_data.name: Clarabell
runners_data.note: Two-year-old who has been absent for 458 days — an enormous layoff — and whose form over 7f-8f on Artificial and Soft gives little confidence for this 6f Good to Firm test; she is a natural back-of-the-field type racing out of that role today, adding further complexity to an already difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent runner who has placed twice at 6f on Good ground and ran 5th in a similar event recently; Orla Tynan claims 7lbs and the horse's consistent ability to hold a decent position makes her a legitimate fringe interest.

runners_data.name: Livingston Range
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who favours hold-up tactics — his two placed efforts both came from the rear — but the density of hold-up runners here means he races further forward than is natural; the tongue-tie is back on and the trainer has had only one winner from three runs in the last fortnight, limiting confidence.

runners_data.name: Run Forrest Run
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose entire recent history is over 7f, dropping back to 6f today in what is a clear trip shortening experiment; he is a genuine hold-up horse racing in a midfield mapping he does not naturally fill, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 accurately reflects the mismatch.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse whose best run — a 2nd over 6f on Good — came from racing prominently on that occasion, suggesting some positional flexibility; the tongue-tie and hood combination is worn, and Terry Casey claims 7lbs, but the redistribution away from his natural last position is a meaningful obstacle in a race this large.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly who fades in the finish consistently and whose best recent result was a 5th over 7f on Good; the fade flag combined with a below-par sim-going record of 0 wins from 5 gives little reason to believe she can overcome a deep draw in a large, competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Kelly is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 6f apprentice handicap and, critically, faces no genuine rival for the lead — she should secure an uncontested rail position and set a sustainable, controlled pace on Good to Firm ground. The prominent brigade of I'm Spartacus, Rappell, Rosato, Whatswrongnow, Hero Of The Hour, Step Back In Time and Jackandthefox will jostle hard behind her in the first furlong, creating a competitive but not frenetic early tempo. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than the pace map can physically accommodate at the rear — Glen Breeze, Monastere, Run Forrest Run, Livingston Range and Clarabell are genuine back-of-the-field horses whose natural habitat is the last quarter of the field, but in a race this busy they will be shuffled even further back than usual, making their tasks harder. With Lady Kelly controlling tempo from the front and likely running conservatively, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the pace — the position immediately behind the leader is the golden draw here, with prominent-style runners who have 6f Good to Firm form the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kelly's controlled lead allows prominent chasers to travel smoothly and pick her off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Lady Kelly's controlled lead allows prominent chasers to travel smoothly and pick her off inside the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kelly's controlled fractions are slow enough that she conserves enough for a genuine final-furlong battle and her rivals fail to close efficiently.
scenarios.body: If Lady Kelly's controlled fractions are slow enough that she conserves enough for a genuine final-furlong battle and her rivals fail to close efficiently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Improvers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot enough to compress the race and allow midfield horses to emerge late between runners.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely hot enough to compress the race and allow midfield horses to emerge late between runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace implodes in the final furlong and the redistributed hold-up types manage to find clear daylight through a wall of tired horses.
scenarios.body: If the pace implodes in the final furlong and the redistributed hold-up types manage to find clear daylight through a wall of tired horses.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kelly (front-runner, sole pace-setter) — watch her early stride pattern; if she bowls along uncontested and reaches halfway with a length advantage intact, prominent chasers will need to be travelling well by the 2f pole to catch her before the line.

I'm Spartacus and Step Back In Time — both have multiple 6f Good-ground form entries and prominent racing styles perfectly suited to this shape; watch where Sam Coen positions I'm Spartacus in the opening 2f, as tracking Lady Kelly's outside could be the race-winning move.

Clarabell (458-day absence) — a two-year-old returning from over a year off into a competitive 18-runner 6f apprentice handicap is a significant fitness concern; watch her in the paddock and early race for any signs of greenness that could compromise her position and that of those drawn nearby.

Traffic risk — with 18 runners, 5+ genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield, and a single front-runner controlling tempo, the straight at Fairyhouse will be a wall of horses at the 2f pole; any horse drawn wide with a prominent style risks being checked at the critical moment of acceleration.

Step Back In Time's headgear (cheekpieces) — retained from the winning run over 6f on Good ground, which is a positive continuity signal; watch whether Chris Timmons' runner travels prominently early, as the style suits the race shape directly.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Tropical Retreat
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D in good ground last season but has had 243 days off and is 10lb higher; Colin Keane takes over and she shapes as a confirmed leader whose ability to dictate a clean, uncontested gallop is the key variable for the whole race.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners a filly with a prominent style who returns just four days after her last run; her true role is racing close to the pace, but with so many similar types in this field she is most at risk of being shuffled back and compromised early.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: Ben Coen and JP Murtagh combine with a filly who has placed six times from her last five runs in similar conditions; races prominently and that profile fits the anticipated shape well, making her one of the primary pace-tracking threats.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a three-year-old who won over this trip in soft ground but whose only good-going placing came at 7f — the step onto faster ground here is worth monitoring, though she races prominently and will be competitive for position from the start.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on a filly absent 285 days and previously campaigned exclusively at 5f; the step up to 6f is unproven and the layoff raises fitness questions, though she is a natural prominent type who could still feature if fit.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners a filly who has placed at this trip on good ground, but her genuine style is prominent racing and Cromwell's yard is 2/33 in the last fortnight; with the prominent slots under pressure she is one of those most likely to be squeezed wider than ideal.

runners_data.name: Beauty Queen
runners_data.note: Holds headgear (p) and has struggled to trouble the judge in recent starts, finishing outside the first seven in each of her last five; her hold-up style leaves her dependent on a strong pace that this race is unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Drops back from 7f-8f trips to 6f and has only one sim-going placing; races from hold-up position and would need a hot pace to land close enough — that pace is unlikely with only one genuine front-runner on show.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Jack Cleary (5) rides a filly who has placed four times in her last five on similar ground and who genuinely wants to come from off the pace; shown in midfield on this map due to redistribution, her natural style is closer to the rear and her chance depends on a stronger gallop than expected.

runners_data.name: Reimagined
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides a three-year-old who wore hood and blinkers last time and won over 6f on good ground; her hold-up style is genuine and she is the most compelling of the closers — she won on this trip and going, making her the most credible beneficiary if the pace does stretch.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a six-year-old wearing a tongue-strap who won over 6f on good ground and has shown placed form in similar conditions; a natural hold-up type placed into midfield by redistribution, her age and recent form profile make her an outsider's prospect at best.

races.paceDynamic: Tropical Retreat is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should bowl along at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over six furlongs at Fairyhouse. Behind her, Glory To Be, Treasure Rose, Thenandnow, and Soulful Diva all want to race prominently, meaning the second and third positions off the pace will be fiercely contested at the start, compressing the field and creating a bunched, moderate-tempo contest rather than a true end-to-end test. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all settle into their natural positions; of those, Treasure Rose and Thenandnow are best-placed by draw, weight, and recency to actually secure prominent berths, while Glory To Be and Treasured Royal are the most likely to be shuffled wider or further back than they prefer. A controlled, single-pacemaker scenario with a compressed mid-pack favours horses who can race handy in the first two or three off the leader and produce a sharp, sustained finish — prominent hold position runners with good recent form on similar ground are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tropical Retreat Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Retreat bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not fierce gallop, rewarding those who track her closely.
scenarios.body: If Tropical Retreat bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not fierce gallop, rewarding those who track her closely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Heats Up
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Treasure Rose, Thenandnow, Soulful Diva — push for position early and lift the pace beyond what Tropical Retreat intended.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of prominent types — Treasure Rose, Thenandnow, Soulful Diva — push for position early and lift the pace beyond what Tropical Retreat intended.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot enough to soften the prominent runners and leave a gap for those held up early.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely hot enough to soften the prominent runners and leave a gap for those held up early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Retreat quickens clear from two furlongs out and the field simply cannot peg her back.
scenarios.body: If Tropical Retreat quickens clear from two furlongs out and the field simply cannot peg her back.

watchPoints.text: Treasure Rose is the most dangerous prominent horse here — JP Murtagh's filly has six places from her last five runs on good ground and is partnered by Ben Coen; if she slots in behind Tropical Retreat she is perfectly positioned to pounce.

Glory To Be and Treasured Royal are both true prominent types and will be fighting for the same limited positions early; watch for either being forced wider or settling further back than intended, which would compromise their chances significantly.

Soulful Diva has been off 285 days and has never raced beyond 5f — if she shows any signs of greenness or blows early, she could unsettle the runners around her as the field jostles for prominent spots behind Tropical Retreat.

Reimagined is the hold-up horse with the most persuasive profile — she won over this exact trip and going and Nathan Crosse rides; if the prominent runners burn each other off at any point, she is the one most likely to produce a sustained late run through the field.

races.name: Racing Again July 8th Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Carrigans Grove
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won on Good going over 6f on most recent start; Carroll in the saddle is a strong pointer, but steps up to 7f for the first time since a win at this trip, and the blinkers are in place — gets a prime stalking pitch if the prominent positions aren't fully taken.

runners_data.name: Little Miss P
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who has been running over longer trips lately (10f, 8f), dropping back to 7f here; visor fitted, 44 days off, and W J Lee aboard, but similar-going record of 0 wins from 6 runs is a major concern.

runners_data.name: Queen Aethelflaed
runners_data.note: Arrived in form with a win two runs back over 8f on Good, now stepping down to 7f; Orla Tynan's 7lb claim is meaningful, trainer Andrew Slattery in a rich 14-day vein of 2 wins from 24, and the tongue-tie is retained — should get a prominent berth naturally.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who scored over 6f on Good 20 days ago; trainer Conor Maxwell has had 1 winner from 4 in the past fortnight and Robert Whearty takes the ride — handles this ground well and drops to 7f after a 6f win, which suits.

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has been running over 7-8f consistently; 44 days since last run is a concern, and the similar-going record of 0 wins from 9 tugs against enthusiasm, even in a wide-open handicap.

runners_data.name: Hasita
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for this race; J P Murtagh's 3-year-old carries the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93), suggesting she is running slightly outside her most natural mode — if she leads on Good to Firm over 7f she controls tempo, but her chance hinges on whether the others let her dominate.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been busy (12 days since last run), has shown place-level form over 7-8f on similar ground, and the tongue-piece and pads (tp) are retained — trainer McGuinness has had 3 winners in 14 days and Adam Caffrey is in decent form.

runners_data.name: Rodeeve
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good 19 days ago and is a genuine hold-up type by nature, though the map places her in midfield given the congestion at the rear; the p-headgear is in place and she handles fast ground well, but her redistribution means she may not get the rearward position she wants.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old from M D O'Callaghan, ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle who is a significant jockey booking; visor worn, only 2 wins from 5 on similar ground but recent 3rd over 7f Good is encouraging for this trip.

runners_data.name: Jasmine Affanalis
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground and is a natural hold-up type by inclination, but the crowded rear means she is shown in midfield; the p-headgear helps concentration and David Marnane's runner brings a 2nd two runs back over 8f Good as her main form reference.

runners_data.name: Mo Anam Chara
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good 44 days ago and this drop back to 7f is the key question; Mark Fahey has been active (3/10 in 14 days), Ronan Whelan is a top booking, and the similar-going record of 1 win from 6 is respectable — gets a natural prominent position.

runners_data.name: Two And Two
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard going and placed at the same trip; stepping up to 7f for the first time is an unknown, and the form string shows inconsistency, but Scott McCullagh has the experience and the trainer has had 1 winner from 9 in the fortnight — capable of running prominently.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old with Colin Keane aboard, which is the stand-out jockey booking in this race; form over 6-8f on similar going shows 0 wins from 4 but Keane knows how to deliver a horse late, and this represents a significant drop in trip to 7f — the class of rider lifts the appeal.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old flagged as fading in the finish; form string of five runs without a win on Good-plus ground and the tendency to fade means fast conditions here are unlikely to reverse that trend — Siobhan Rutledge has a difficult task.

runners_data.name: Elly Bay
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer by inclination but the volume of front-runners in this field means she is mapped to midfield, carrying a STYLE_FIT flag; her best form includes a 2nd over 7f Good and 3rd over 8f Good, so the trip is fine, but James Ryan will find it hard to get a forward position.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 7f on Good going (form: 222915 — the 1 was 19 days ago), a genuine hold-up type who is placed further forward on the map due to traffic at the rear; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps the weight, but the redistribution means she may not find the clear run she ideally wants.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount is a natural prominent racer whose crowded field means she has been mapped to midfield despite her style; form shows a 3rd over 8f on Heavy and 4th over 8f Good, so stepping down to 7f is a question, and Mrs Harrington's trainer has been busy (6/37 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Casla's Eagle
runners_data.note: Unknown style (tagged U) with only three career runs and 57 days off the track; limited form on similar going (1 run from 3) makes assessment difficult, but Chris Hayes is a capable jockey and Peter Fahey a shrewd handler — watch for any market support.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Hold-up type rated 71 (top weight here) and 53 days since last run; visor fitted, ran 3rd over 7f on Heavy previously which is her best, and W McCreery's stable has had 1 winner from 10 in the fortnight — the weight and layoff stack up as negatives.

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Prominent 5-year-old who has won twice on similar ground, including a 3rd over 8f Good recently; Ross O'Sullivan has sent out 4 winners from 21 runners in 14 days, and Donagh O'Connor gets the ride — the hood is retained and she carries joint-top weight of 144lbs.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who has won over 6f Good and placed over 7f Good, but the field's surfeit of prominent types means she is mapped to midfield; no jockey declared yet is a flag, and the 3-year-old's redistribution means she is unlikely to secure the prominent berth that showcases her best form.

races.paceDynamic: Hasita is the confirmed front-runner here, and on Good to Firm ground over 7f at Fairyhouse she is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without a serious challenger for the lead — her pace tag and STYLE_FIT flag both suggest she is racing slightly outside her most natural comfort zone, but she is still likely to sit in front and control tempo. Behind her, a cluster of prominent-types — Carrigans Grove, Queen Aethelflaed, Are You In Or Out, Mo Anam Chara, Two And Two, Minaun View, and Altimara — will be competing for the front rank, and with several unable to get their natural position, a degree of early jostling is inevitable even if the pace itself remains measured. The hold-up contingent — including Sagasti, Caitouna, Bundle Of Interest, and Little Miss P — will be last to show their hand, but a sustainable rather than scorching gallop on quick ground may not fully suit horses coming from deep. This race shape, with a single controlled pace-setter and a congested midfield, most favours horses who can sit prominently just off the leader and quicken from a handy position in the final two furlongs; the field contains more prominent types than the map can accommodate, and Carrigans Grove, Queen Aethelflaed, and Mo Anam Chara are most likely to actually secure those coveted stalking positions behind Hasita, while Bear Right, Elly Bay, and Dervo Annie may be squeezed wider or further back than they would prefer.

scenarios.body: If Hasita sets a fair but sustainable gallop and horses who track her from second or third are able to challenge in the final furlong.

scenarios.body: If Hasita is allowed to go entirely unchallenged and steals a march that cannot be bridged by the trailing pack on quick ground.

scenarios.title: Redistribution Creates Chaos

scenarios.body: If the over-supply of prominent types causes significant early interference, wide draws, or pace collapse and produces a messy, hard-to-read finish.

watchPoints.text: Caitouna — Colin Keane's booking stands out in a wide-open handicap; watch how he positions this hold-up filly in the run and whether she shows any signs of an each-way market move before the off.

Queen Aethelflaed — trainer Andrew Slattery is in form (2/24 in 14 days) and Orla Tynan's 7lb claim is real value; she should secure a prominent pitch naturally and the combination of claim, form, and trip drop makes her highly relevant.

Prominent-type traffic early — Bear Right, Elly Bay, and Dervo Annie cannot all get their natural positions behind Hasita; watch for crowding, bumping, or wide tracking in the early stages which could compromise multiple runners' chances.

races.name: GAIN The Advantage Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a notable fade tendency; best form on Soft (1W in similar going on Flat) and all three Good-ground runs at 8f have produced double-figure finishes — the Good to Firm at 1m½f does not flatter this profile.

runners_data.name: Fortuity
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; Shane Foley can control every yard of this race on Good to Firm ground where the horse is 1W2P in 7 starts, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reminds us this is a horse racing in its preferred position only because no rival challenges — the handicapper's weight may still catch it.

runners_data.name: Hippology
runners_data.note: Held up by Joseph O'Brien, returning after 57 days off with a fade flag attached; both Good-ground runs have yielded finishes of 16th and 5th, and the extended layoff combined with a poor recent form string (5-00) makes confidence hard to build.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Style unknown, which gives Ronan Whelan tactical flexibility; placed third last time at 8f on Good for Fahey whose yard is 0/9 in the last 14 days — form is modest but the unknown style tag means it could land anywhere in the field.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Returned from 210 days off to win impressively on the AW for O'Sullivan; hood worn, and that sharp form needs to translate to turf Good to Firm at 1m½f — the stamina question is real given most of its best form came over shorter on AW.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Unknown style, one of Noel Meade's stable, but all five career runs have produced finishes between 4th and 9th; blinkers worn and the step up to 1m½f Good to Firm on a track where she has no previous form makes this a speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature — Wesley Joyce (3) takes the ride — whose true rear-of-field style is compressed to midfield on the map because the field is so full of closers; STYLE_FIT 0.90 underlines it will struggle to get its natural position, and 0/5 in similar going is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on a horse with a win and a place in its last five, but its authentic hold-up profile is squeezed forward on the map by sheer field congestion; six furlongs to seven furlongs has been its comfort zone and the step to 1m½f remains an open question.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides a Joseph O'Brien hold-up type at 1m½f, a trip it has tried once (7th over 12f); form figures of 0757 are modest but the trainer-jockey combination is live and Good ground suits (3/4 similar-going runs placed).

runners_data.name: Avoca Woods
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's runner carries a fade flag and its hold-up style is pushed into midfield on the map — the three career runs have all ended in single-figure finishes but nothing near the frame; STYLE_FIT 0.90 suggests it will not reproduce its natural racing pattern here.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places in 14 similar-going runs, giving it the best strike rate in going-matched conditions in the field; Adam Browne-Souza (7) claims, and the hold-up style is genuinely compressed to midfield by a field stacked with closers — a cleaner run would suit more than it is likely to get.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: Unknown style for W McCreery; three career runs have all returned 6th, 6th, 8th — consistency of mid-table mediocrity — and the yard is 1/13 in the last fortnight, making this a fringe interest at best.

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up filly, Gary Carroll aboard; every career start has finished 7th or 8th, showing a pattern of running no race, and being remapped to midfield from her natural position at the rear compounds rather than helps her situation.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's second string (also trains Only One Scobie); tongue-tied and with a fade flag, five of six runs have been in the 9th-15th range — one win at 1m on AW is the sole bright spot and Good to Firm turf at 1m½f represents a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Schoolyard Days
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners this M C Grassick hold-up type, fitted with a hood; form of 60-858 and a natural rear-of-field style that the congested map cannot place honestly at the back — STYLE_FIT 0.90 confirms it will not travel in its preferred spot, and the lowest OR in the field (50) reflects the mountain to climb.

races.paceDynamic: Fortuity is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner handicap over 1m½f at Fairyhouse on Good to Firm ground, and with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Shane Foley can control tempo from the front without being pressured — a genuinely unchallenged pace that is likely to be honest rather than suicidal. The field is loaded with hold-up types, but so many genuine closers are competing for the same late ground that they will cannibalize one another's finishing lanes, particularly at a track where position off the turn matters. Kc Bear, Cisterna, Jp's Express, Retro Gal, Dawn Flame, Schoolyard Days and Avoca Woods are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate them all at the rear — in practice, several will be trapped in traffic at the critical moment. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can track Fortuity at a sustainable clip and pounce turning in, rather than deep closers who need clear daylight that may never come in such a congested field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fortuity Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Fortuity bowls along at a fair but unforced gallop and prominent/mid-division trackers make smooth progress from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Fortuity bowls along at a fair but unforced gallop and prominent/mid-division trackers make smooth progress from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop, Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Fortuity goes faster than expected and the pace proves genuinely testing over 1m½f, creating enough of a speed-burn to release the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Fortuity goes faster than expected and the pace proves genuinely testing over 1m½f, creating enough of a speed-burn to release the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fortuity Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Fortuity is allowed to coast on a very modest pace and never faced down, turning a 1m½f handicap into a test of stamina over rivals who cannot close the gap.
scenarios.body: If Fortuity is allowed to coast on a very modest pace and never faced down, turning a 1m½f handicap into a test of stamina over rivals who cannot close the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers Outrun Style
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the redistributed horses manages to secure an uncharacteristically forward position and avoids the hold-up traffic entirely.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the redistributed horses manages to secure an uncharacteristically forward position and avoids the hold-up traffic entirely.

watchPoints.text: Fortuity (Shane Foley) must be tracked from the break — if Foley drops in quietly rather than bowling along, the pace becomes dangerously slow and the entire field compresses, wiping out any clearer-air advantage for the trackers.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Cisterna, Kc Bear, Jp's Express, Retro Gal, Dawn Flame, Schoolyard Days, Avoca Woods) will all be jostling for limited room on the rail at halfway — watch for traffic jams turning out of the back straight that could eliminate several at once.

John La Bear (Donagh O'Connor) is returning from 210 days off following an AW win; if it handles the turf-to-Good to Firm switch after a long layoff it could outrun its odds, but any sluggishness at the start will bury it in the back of a 15-runner cavalry charge.

Kc Bear (Colin Keane) is the most notable jockey upgrade in the field — Keane rarely rides in handicaps of this level without a live chance, and if the horse manages to secure a position closer to the pace than its natural style suggests, the STYLE_FIT discount becomes less relevant.

Going described as Good to Firm throughout the card but listed as Good in the race conditions — confirm official description at post time, as any overnight moisture softening the ground meaningfully would shift the advantage toward horses with better Soft/Good form such as Only One Scobie and Cisterna.

races.name: Early Bird Winter Festival Tickets At Fairyhouse.ie Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with solid form at this trip and going combination (1W1P in similar conditions), W J Lee partners her and she has winning form over 8f on good; the most credible late finisher if any pace materialises, but faces an uphill task if Blue Anthem is allowed a soft lead.

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter and naturally prominent, though a STYLE_FIT flag notes the position may be mildly out of role; ran just yesterday which is a major concern for fitness and durability, and his 0W2P record on similar going reflects a horse who performs respectably but is not a certainty to last home.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in the finish and carries a headgear note (tongue-tie, pads); his trip form is mixed (has run over both shorter and longer), and with 13 days since his last run he arrives fresh but his finishing tendency makes this moderate-pace scenario unfavourable.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who won over 8f on good and carries Colin Keane, one of the highest-quality jockey bookings in the race; headgear (pads) worn and 20 days since his last run — if anyone is going to press Blue Anthem it is him, and Keane will know exactly when to pounce.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner stepping up slightly from his recent 7f form, which has returned no wins or places on any going; the 7lb claimer Jimmy Dalton reduces the weight burden but the lack of a place in recent outings and soft-ground background make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Placed at 8f on good ground and wears a tongue-tie and pads combination; trainer Patrick T Foley has two wins from seven in the past 14 days suggesting decent current form, and his natural prominent style places him near the action — consistent without being a winner.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who fades in the finish and has very limited form on good going (1 from 8 runs in similar conditions); the 3lb claimer Kearney lightens the load but the going stats and finishing tendency make a big run unlikely in this shape.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has only three career starts, all on going softer than today; held up and lightly raced, 57 days since last appearance — raw and untested on this surface, his chance is difficult to assess but the form profile is thin.

runners_data.name: Believeth
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie, has a genuine hold-up profile, and is mapped to midfield because of the volume of backmarkers in this field — but make no mistake, this horse wants to be last and come late; on good-to-firm he has posted a modest 3/5 position record and with a fade-in-finish flag, the pace scenario is working against him.

runners_data.name: Milverton
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse over middle distances, his last five runs include several on good-to-good-firm ground (including a place at 10f on good) but he has been shuffled into midfield on the map purely due to congestion at the rear; the STYLE_FIT flag applies, he will struggle to find his true rhythm in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: Off for 231 days, a very significant absence for any horse in a competitive handicap; wears a tongue-tie and his three career runs have returned no wins or places — the race-rustiness combined with a true hold-up style that cannot be deployed naturally here makes this a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up gelding wearing a hood, with 26 days since his last outing; his record on good ground shows 11 from 15 runs finishing outside the places, and with a fade-in-finish flag and redistribution off the rear of the field, the race shape is not in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Anthem is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo over this 1m½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Fairyhouse. Launch Time and Pete's Dream will press from a prominent position, but neither is a natural pace-setter and both are likely to settle just off the leader rather than push for the front, meaning Blue Anthem dictates rhythm without being harassed. The hold-up brigade — Bella Colombia, Milverton, Believeth, Tullyesker, Rushford, Heart of Darkness and others — are extremely numerous, and with multiple true closers redistributed into midfield on the map, not all can find their natural rear-of-field spot; Milverton and Believeth are among the least likely to operate from their ideal position. A sustainable, moderate gallop with a single pace-setter is the probable shape, and this setup strongly favours prominent-to-mid horses who can travel close enough to challenge in the straight without needing a true searching pace to reel back the leader — hold-up specialists dependent on a genuine burn face the added risk that the fractions are simply too honest for a late rattle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blue Anthem Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Anthem is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo and neither Launch Time nor Pete's Dream presses to within a length of him in the first half-mile.
scenarios.body: If Blue Anthem is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo and neither Launch Time nor Pete's Dream presses to within a length of him in the first half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Run Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time or Pete's Dream races closer than expected to Blue Anthem and the tempo lifts enough to bring the prominent types into play in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Launch Time or Pete's Dream races closer than expected to Blue Anthem and the tempo lifts enough to bring the prominent types into play in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely hotts up from halfway and the leaders burn each other out, leaving a gap for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: If the pace genuinely hotts up from halfway and the leaders burn each other out, leaving a gap for the backmarkers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Anthem goes too slowly and the entire field bunches together, turning the race into a sprint off a crawl.
scenarios.body: If Blue Anthem goes too slowly and the entire field bunches together, turning the race into a sprint off a crawl.

watchPoints.text: Blue Anthem ran only yesterday — monitor for signs of fatigue or reduced fluency in the closing stages, as a tired front-runner could dramatically alter the finish.

Launch Time with Colin Keane could push harder for the lead than expected if Keane judges the pace too slow; if he goes after Blue Anthem early, the entire pace dynamic shifts and the race becomes a test of stamina.

Bella Colombia is the stand-out hold-up runner on going figures but requires a genuine pace to close into — watch whether any prominent horse has enough gas to keep the tempo honest through the final three furlongs.

The weight of redistributed hold-up horses (Milverton, Believeth, Tullyesker, Rushford, Heart of Darkness) means the field is likely to fan wide in the straight as jockeys hunt daylight — runners on the outside rail in the final two furlongs may find easier ground.

Tullyesker's 231-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race; watch how sharply he surfaces from the stalls and whether he travels freely in the early stages, as any sluggishness would confirm he needs the run.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran returning after 224 days off for D Buckley; form entirely over 16f and in similar going conditions but zero wins or placed runs in simulated good ground runs, and as a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by the race shape, the lay-off and redistribution both work against her.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins runner 13 days fresh with a form line showing double-figure finishes over marathon trips on good and heavy ground; she is a genuine hold-up type who gets her natural position but her record in similar going (8th of 15 on best comparable run) gives little confidence at this trip.

runners_data.name: Altura
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's lightly raced three-year-old with just one run (7th over 10f on good) and 77 days off; a natural closer whose race position will be compromised by the crowded hold-up contingent, so Shane Foley will need to find a clear run from what will effectively be a midfield slot.

runners_data.name: Cosmetic
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien filly with headgear (p) switching for the first time, showing recent form of 5-5-7-9 mostly on soft or heavy surfaces; the step up to 14f for Wayne Lordan is unproven and her hold-up style placing her in midfield rather than her preferred rear means this trip on faster ground is a genuine double question mark.

runners_data.name: Essential Comedy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unbeaten unknown quantity for Claire O'Connell with Colin Keane booked — a significant jockey booking for a yard with modest strike rate; only one run to assess (6th over 13f on good) but the unknown style tag means Keane can place her tactically, which matters greatly in this bunched shape.

runners_data.name: French Blond
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old with a single run (8th over 10f on good, 65 days ago); a true hold-up performer who will be jostling for space in a compressed midfield rather than tracking from the rear where she would ideally race, so her debut experience counts for little in predicting how she handles the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Invincible Destiny
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's second runner, sole outing was 12th of 12 on heavy ground over 12f — both the going and track conditions were entirely different; although a natural closer, the redistribution into midfield and that uninspiring debut make it very difficult to project a step forward significant enough to threaten here.

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner for W McCreery with WJ Lee up, wearing a tongue tie; her two runs have come on soft and good going over 10f where she finished 9th and 10th, yet her confirmed lead style in a field of closers hands her a tactical golden opportunity over this extended 14f trip on drying ground.

runners_data.name: Pleased
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's filly with back-to-back placed runs (2nd and 3rd) over 12f on good ground with Dylan Browne McMonagle retained — the most meaningful form line in the race; her consistent finishing positions suggest she can travel prominently from a flexible position and her proven course-trip-going profile makes her the most complete package.

runners_data.name: Soigne
runners_data.note: Second Gavin Cromwell runner alongside French Blond, lightly exposed with one run (9th over 10f on good); Gary Carroll takes the ride but there is very little to work with here, and a true hold-up style means she faces the same positional compromise as her stablemate without any advantage in form or experience.

runners_data.name: Spry
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John McConnell with Siobhan Rutledge; going preference is unknown (tagged turf-only) and no form to assess — pure unknown quantity, but the fact that her style is also unclassified means the jockey can position her wherever the race dictates, which could be an inadvertent advantage in this congested shape.

runners_data.name: Vanir
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's filly for Ben Coen showed a placed run (2nd over 10f on good) followed by an 8th — the first run the more encouraging; her hold-up style gets her natural position more cleanly than most rivals here and the step up to 14f on similar going could unlock improvement, making her one of the more credible closers in the field.

runners_data.name: Werifesteria
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's third runner, fitted with a hood (p), sole start was 7th over 12f on standard Dundalk — the all-weather form is essentially incomparable to this good to firm turf test; Scott McCullagh rides and the unfamiliar surface combined with a hold-up style in a crowded rear group makes meaningful assessment very difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Path To Peace is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f — this is not a pressured lead, it is a controlled solo dictation. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types, and the redistribution note is significant: Keep It Together, French Blond, Invincible Destiny and Cosmetic are all genuine closers who cannot all find their natural rear position and will be shuffled into midfield instead. That compression of hold-up horses into the middle of the pack reduces the likelihood of a clean late sweep and instead creates a bunched mid-race scenario where position and cover matter enormously. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind Path To Peace and quicken from a stalking position — in this field, that points clearly to horses with unknown or flexible style profiles (Pleased, Essential Comedy, Spry) who can sit second or third and pounce, or genuine hold-up horses with strong finishing form who survive the redistribution chaos.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Lead Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Path To Peace bowls along uncontested and the chasing pack fails to close the gap until too late.
scenarios.body: If Path To Peace bowls along uncontested and the chasing pack fails to close the gap until too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a flexible or prominent-tracking horse sits second or third throughout and picks off a tiring Path To Peace inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a flexible or prominent-tracking horse sits second or third throughout and picks off a tiring Path To Peace inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution chaos resolves cleanly and a genuine closer threads through the bunched midfield to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution chaos resolves cleanly and a genuine closer threads through the bunched midfield to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses Quickly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves misleadingly slow early and then quickens sharply in the straight, catching the bunched midfield flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves misleadingly slow early and then quickens sharply in the straight, catching the bunched midfield flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Path To Peace (WJ Lee) sets the tempo from the front completely unchallenged — watch whether Lee elects to steal a march turning for home, as any increase in the gallop at the 3f pole could make this race almost impossible to win from off the pace.

The redistribution of Keep It Together, French Blond, Invincible Destiny and Cosmetic into midfield creates a serious traffic-jam scenario in the straight — watch for significant interference between the 2f and 1f poles as multiple hold-up horses attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Pleased (Dylan Browne McMonagle) is the form pick on paper but watch her starting price — if heavily backed she will be a target for market movers and her position directly behind Path To Peace in the early stages is crucial; if she gets shuffled back into the melee her task becomes markedly harder.

Essential Comedy with Colin Keane booked for a lightly raced filly from a small yard is a notable jockey-booking angle — watch the market move at the off, as Keane rarely accepts rides of this nature without intelligence suggesting the filly is more forward than her single run implies.

Spry is an unraced unknown with an unclassified style — watch her in the parade ring and at the start for any signs of greenness or market support, as debut runners from the McConnell yard on turf can occasionally spring a surprise when freshness counts over 14f on good ground.
